title: Entropy heuristics for LM probes and calibration
content:
Purpose / why I care:
- Quick, lightweight heuristics to detect when an LLM answer is likely low-quality or OOD without heavy evals.
- Want something that can run in-stream in Redwood hosted API, or as a cheap post-check in Dedicated/private deployments.

Reading list (skim + mental notes):
- "On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks" (Guo et al., 2017) — calibration gaps exist even when accuracy high. Key idea: naive softmax probs != calibrated confidence.
- "Deep Ensembles" (Lakshminarayanan et al., 2017) — ensembles as simple uncertainty estimator; good but expensive for serving.
- "Entropy as a proxy for epistemic uncertainty" (various blog posts 2026-2028) — per-token entropy drift often correlates with hallucination windows. Need to validate for long contexts.
- "Detecting Out-of-Distribution Inputs in Language Models" (workshop papers 2028-2029) — use internal logits, top-k mass, and KL to baseline to flag OOD.

Notes / distilled heuristics I want to test quickly:
1) Rolling-token-entropy: compute mean token entropy over sliding window (w=8/16/32 tokens). Sudden spike correlates with hallucinations.
2) Top-k mass collapse: fraction of mass in top-1/top-5 tokens. If top-1 mass drops below threshold for many tokens -> model is uncertain / drifting.
3) Prefix-context KL: compare current token distribution to distribution conditioned on a short generic baseline prompt (e.g., "The following text is about"). Large KL suggests novel context.
4) Logit gap: difference between top-1 and top-2 logits (pre-softmax). Small gap often means ambiguous continuation.
5) Cross-turn entropy shift: measure entropy change between user-turn and assistant-turn tokens to capture info-loss in generation.

Datasets / testbeds to use (cheap and fast):
- Red-team prompt corpus (internal): mix of adversarial prompts, nonsense, long-chain reasoning tasks.
- TriviaQA / NaturalQuestions slices with truncated contexts to simulate partial info.
- Human-labeled hallucination set from prior incident logs (CS) — useful for real-world signal.

Metrics to instrument:
- Precision/recall of flagging on known hallucination windows.
- False positive rate on benign system outputs (chit-chat, code completion).
- Latency overhead: target <1ms/token additional in pipeline (approx).
- Correlation with downstream quality metrics (human rating, BLEU-ish for QA).

Mini-experiment plan (week 1):
- Implement streaming entropy calc in JS/Go shim that wraps Redwood SDK. Make it batch-friendly.
- Run on 10k batched completions from hosted-api logs (anonymized) and compute the heuristics above per token.
- Label samples: use the internal heuristic label from safety pipeline + random human spot-checks.
- Produce PR with result artifacts: histograms, ROC curves, examples of true/false positives.

Pseudocode sketch (streaming-friendly):
- For each incoming token logits:
  - compute softmax probs (numerically stable), entropy H = -sum p log p
  - compute topk_mass = sum_{i<=k} p_i
  - compute logit_gap = z_1 - z_2 (z = logits)
  - push into circular buffer of size W, compute rolling mean/std of H and topk_mass
  - trigger alert if rolling H > mean_H + alpha * std_H OR topk_mass < tau_k for t consecutive tokens

Open questions / concerns:
- Temperature / sampling affects logits/probs for sampled tokens — need to compute metrics on raw logits before sampling (we have access in runtime?). If not, approximate via importance.
- Quantization: int8/4-bit kernels might change logits slightly — do metrics still hold? Need to test with Dedicated/Private stacks.
- Adaptive thresholds per model/sequence-length/regulatory tenant? Probably necessary.
- Canary vs universal thresholds: we could auto-calibrate per model by logging a 24h baseline. Privacy/RTO implications.

Potential product hooks: 
- "uncertainty flag" field in response envelope that apps can use to trigger fallback (search, rerank, conservative wording).
- Console dashboard showing entropy heatmaps across routes/models.
- A/B test: baseline vs uncertainty-aware fallback on customer-facing help bot. Measure reduction in hallucination complaints.

Next actions (todo):
- [ ] Implement proof-of-concept shim + collect 10k examples (by 2029-12-13)
- [ ] Confirm access to raw logits in hosted-api pipeline with infra (ping: infra#logits-access)
- [ ] Run small quantization sensitivity test on local quantized runtime (ping: Mika)
- [ ] Draft short Internals note with sample flagged transcripts for Console UX team

Quick examples (hand-picked):
- Prompt: "Explain why Pluto is a planet." -> generation devolves into confident-sounding wrong facts. Entropy trace: low then sudden spike at divergence.
- Prompt: "Translate idiom: \"break the ice\" into X-language (low-resource)" -> high entropy throughout; topk_mass low; suggests fallback to retrieval or abstain.

Notes-to-self: keep thresholds conservative initially to avoid user-facing churn. Emphasize "assistive" warnings rather than hard failures. Record calibration-run nightly and store aggregate stats in S3 path: s3://redwood-research/entropy-baselines/2029-12/

Questions for collaborators:
- Ravi: can we instrument logits in the hosted path without perf cliff?
- Mika: benchmark on quantized kernels — do you expect entropy statistics to shift systematically?

End-of-file — this is a sketchy, iterative doc. Will refine after first run and make a nicer Tech Note if signals look promising.
